$latePlug: Delayed-plug thread format (owner 2026-11-25, late-plug.mjs, docs/late-plug.md). The thread ships with no plug and ends on its last point; its heavy block waits as a [LATE PLUG of <id>] draft and is replied under the thread's last tweet when the thread has momentum. Owner 2026-11-25 "It should be at the level of t2": fire at Fuel's T2 bar, velocityAt views/hour only (viewsAt null = off), never before minAgeH; velocity = slope between hourly FxTwitter reads, else the average since posting; every thread is plugged by fallbackH (T2's 6h window) whatever its views, so none ships unmonetized; giveUpH = Telegram alert when FxTwitter never answers.
$comment: THE single source of numeric law. Every gate, planner, prompt and audit READS this file; none restates it. Born 2026-08-18 after sixteen instruction-vs-check contradictions in two days, every one caused by the same rule retyped in two places that then drifted apart. A rule change is an edit HERE and nowhere else. Prose docs cite the key path (laws.json: tweet.maxThread), never the number.

tweet.$rhythm: Operator 2026-09-13, writing the first remix by hand: "make sure none of our sentences are too long. Goal is to make it skimmable, so spacing + variety in sentence length" and "bar the listicle, I want no more than 4 paragraphs. Ideally it's between 3 - 4." The ceiling is 17, set 2026-09-15 from the operator's own FINISHED remix (burner draft 10750363 — the other nine were iterations toward it, not ten remixes): 45 sentences, median 10w, p75 13w, p90 16w, true max 17w once the compliance tweet is excluded. "~15" is the centre they write around; 17 is the edge they actually reach. At 15 the check flags five deliberate lines of their best work, which is how an advisory gets ignored. maxSentenceWords counts only segments that END in terminal punctuation — an item title line and an inline bullet row are not sentences. maxParagraphs counts blank-line-separated blocks; a numbered listicle item is exempt, per "bar the listicle".
tweet.$citationTweetsMax: SOURCES SUPPORT THE WRITING, THEY DO NOT REPLACE IT (operator, 2026-09-23: 'Make sure we don't fall into the issue of being too clever anding adding sources for everything. I think it kind of destroy the old linguistic fingerprint. Add where it's needed and support the writing, not overused.'). The mock run's cover carried an academic parenthetical, (Name et al., 2018), in 7 of 11 body tweets and read like a paper, not the page. Where a claim came from belongs in draft.sources, which the Typefully note shows under CLAIMS; the copy names a source only where the claim leans on it, in the page's own words. More tweets than this carrying a paper-style citation is flagged to the owner (review, never a hold).

hook.$remixLane: A REMIX IS EXEMPT FROM coverFloor, and for the opposite reason to a harvest (operator 2026-09-17, planning Run 5's 20/20 cover-remix split). A harvest has no donor hook at all. A remix HAS one and keeps only its SHAPE — remix-thread's layer 1 is the promise mechanic, layer 3 is the topic and every word of it, and layer 3 is written fresh — so a remix hook is supposed to share almost nothing with the donor's wording and coverFloor would refuse the lane by construction. The similarity is still MEASURED and still rides the ledger row, so the next autopsy can ask what remix fidelity does to reach; it simply does not decide whether the thread ships. Before this, the only remixes that ever shipped did it by leaving recId blank on the burner, which passes the gate as "unmeasured" — a gate disabled by an empty field. What a remix still owes is layer 2: the count (hookPromiseIssue), the audience filter verbatim, the tension direction and the authority stance.
hook.$coverFloor: Operator 2026-09-06, after the Sep 4-6 autopsy (37 of 47 covers below 0.72; median views 79K against 1.43M in band, an 18x gap on the same pages and fuel): a COVER ships only at >= coverFloor of its donor hook. Between gateMin and coverFloor it ships only with a declared drift class on the spec (hookDrift: { class, note }), class one of driftClasses. Below gateMin nothing ships. Above gateMax is a duplicate post. publish-thread is the gate, hooks-check the dashboard; harvests, pots, seeds and the burner are exempt (no donor hook to keep).
hook.$hardClaimClass: THE FIFTH CLASS, added 2026-09-17. The other four all say the same thing in different words: the donor's hook contains something this fleet cannot reproduce in its own voice. A HARD HEALTH CLAIM is exactly that and had no escape, so a donor whose hook says "reverse" or "cure" could not be covered faithfully at all — keeping the hook ships a claim hardHealthClaim blocks, and cutting the word drops the similarity under coverFloor. Measured across the 1,095-day pool on the day it was added: 15 of 878 usable donors, 1.7%, among them a 2.5M Stanford cartilage thread and a 4.8M grey-hair thread. Small, real, and previously unreachable. The note must name the word that was dropped and what replaced it, because that is the whole content of the declaration.
hook.$leadItem: A numbered first tweet leads with the list's strongest item (lead-item.mjs). Owner, 2026-09-28, asking "is it possible to lead the tweet 1 in a numbered thread with the most clickbaiting point first? Is that quantifiable with Jev. Contrarian could be considered.", then, after the retro test: "yes adopt fully — every numbered first tweet should have it implemented." Evidence (learnings/lead-item.md, our 612 numbered first tweets over 90 days): item 1 as the list's top-pull item reached 100k views 56% vs 41%, 1.69x page median views, same money per view; with item 1 out of sight in tweet 2 the split shows nothing (29% vs 28%). Jev reads each item alone under the hook (lead-pull-read); another item that beats item 1 by margin trades places with it, every word kept (a swap, not a move to the front: a move pushed the first ask past tweet 4 in all 19 moves on the last run). The last item, an item carrying a link, an item that shares a tweet or runs on, and an item opening on a connective never lead. minItems: a list shorter than this is left alone.
hook.$leadItemGuards: Owner, 2026-09-29, asked whether to remove these so every numbered first tweet swaps: "keep the exceptions". Two reads keep a list whole (lead-item.mjs): a list Jev reads as a sequence at orderedMax or above keeps its order (steps, a story told in order, a morning/lunch/night stack: 19 of the 270 would-be moves in the retro corpus), and a move that would separate an item from a neighbour leaning on it at followMax or above is skipped for the next strongest item ("Remember, don't take the wrong form." after "Magnesium Glycinate": 45 of the 270). Set to 1 to switch a guard off.

scale.$comment: Scaling-phase knobs (operator 2026-08-25). Growing the fleet must never need a code edit: the planner, winner rule, harvest and blitz read these plus the LIVE roster. winClicks counts LIFETIME LEVANTA clicks; winRevenue lifetime commission. DEPRECATED PAIR (2026-09-02): winClicks/winRevenue backed the retired Winner/Repost Candidate statuses — the `farm` block's gates are the successor; existing readers keep working but nothing new should consume these two.
scale.$sellSlotBoost: A donor that monetized its OWN thread hands us the position the creator already conversion-tested; our plug replaces theirs in place. Measured 2026-08-28: 56 of 85 usable donors in the window carry one, and they are the highest-value shape we harvest.
scale.$roundupBoost: Three or more bridgeable substances means the roundup rule allows one plug per product instead of two, so the slot is worth roughly double. Rare: 1 in 40 of the recent top donors.
scale.$topMoldExtraSlots: Extra weekly slots the best-CONVERTING proven mold gets, per account (operator 2026-08-25). 0 restores the flat rotation. Ranked on clicksPer100k over molds.json measured, so it only moves once a mold has a real sample.

farm.$comment: The Cover -> Harvest -> Seed gates (operator, 2026-09-01 doc + session). Every figure is LIFETIME and clicks are LEVANTA lifetime clicks (the registry's Lifetime Clicks column), never Typefully's. Entry gate passes on ANY of four paths: gateViews+gateCommission, gateViews+gateClicks (Levanta), gateViews+gateTypefullyClicks (the same-day sensor, added 2026-09-16 so a body with broken Levanta attribution is not invisible), or gateStraightCommission alone (no view floor — money is the point). harvest-gate.mjs is the only referee; registry-sync is the sensor; Airtable stores state and never computes it.
farm.$gateTypefullyClicks: A FOURTH entry path, on the click figure the registry already stores as `Link Clicks` (the MAX of Typefully's and Levanta's sensors). Levanta measures affiliate clicks that reached the destination and settles late; Typefully measures every link click in the thread and settles same-day. Measured 2026-09-16 over 1,094 published rows: the per-post Levanta/Typefully ratio has median 0.676 and the money-weighted ratio is 0.723 ($0.4692 per Levanta click against $0.3391 per Typefully click), so gateClicks 600 lands at 830-888 by ratio; a threshold sweep over the 146 posts past the view floor puts precision = recall = 0.805 at 900. ADDITIVE, never a replacement: 21 posts past the view floor carry real Typefully clicks and ZERO Levanta attribution (14,767 clicks between them), and 8 of those clear 900 — bodies the clicks path structurally cannot see.
farm.$potentialFloor: Watchlist tier: >= this lifetime commission but not yet gate-passing. Auto-promotes the moment a gate path clears — no operator action needed.
farm.$tiers: By settled tracked commission: T1 tier1Min..tier2Min, T2 tier2Min..tier3Min, T3 above. Clicks-path entrants below tier1Min sit Untiered until data settles.
farm.$hearts: Each heart is a verbatim repost with a fresh link. Two distinct repeats at 70% of the STANDARD entry thresholds qualify for Seed-Eligible: 280K views + $175 commission, 280K + 420 clicks, or $280 commission. Original performance does not count as a repeat. Origin entry and pot thresholds remain unchanged. The operator names and approves seeds.
farm.$cooldownHours: The ONLY spacing rule: one body never posts twice fleet-wide inside this window.
farm.$verdictProvisionalHours: A perform can be awarded after 48h from publication. A miss also waits for the publication UTC day to close plus reportSettlementHours, because Levanta ingests daily earnings late. Later lifetime accrual can promote Missed to Performed.
farm.$repost: A CREATOR REPOSTS THEIR OWN WINNER, and the second post gets a new tweet id. harvest-classify's donor key is the full source URL, so those two reads as two donor threads and the covers of them fragment into two Harvest bodies — each auditing alone on its own hearts, each needing its own performsToSeed. Measured on the live pool 2026-09-18: @coachwillstone's 'Your blood sugar is aging you faster than smoking/cigarettes' is one thread posted twice, holding 8 spent hearts and $1,827 across two rows at 0 performs each, with the denser row already at the heart cap — it would have Retired without ever being seed-eligible. So a donor HANDLE plus a near-verbatim hook links unattended too. The bar is measured, not chosen: across every live pair, same-handle hook affinity tops out at 0.89 and the NEXT same-handle pair sits at 0.67, while the highest CROSS-handle pair in the whole pool is 0.33. 0.85 sits in that gap; it merges the one real repost and nothing else, and no cross-creator pair comes within 0.5 of it.
farm.$harvestEditMax: A HARVEST MAY BE LIGHTLY EDITED (operator, 2026-09-23: 'we can make a rule where if we change less than 5% of a thread it's still considered a harvest. Relatively we should keep the hook the same.'). A verbatim body that a reviewer holds for one false line or one broken step can be repaired in place and still spend its heart as a harvest, instead of being dropped. Measured in WORDS: the word-level edit distance (insertions, deletions, substitutions; a tweet break counts as a word) between the source body and the copy, divided by the source's word count, with tracking links neutralised and the page sign-off (closing, disclaimer, site line) left out. It must be strictly BELOW this share, and tweet 1 (the hook) must be unchanged. At or above it, or with any hook change, the row is a harvest VARIATION, not an attempt. Every edit under the bar is still put to the owner with its percentage. Raised from 0.05 to 0.075 by the owner on 2026-09-23 ('we can move the similarity percentage to 7.5% if needed'): the julian repost needed 7.1% to fix two repeated tweets.
farm.$pots: Seed children, operator-written via /pot: potChances attempts each, perform >= once at potGateFactor x the full gate. A pot clearing the FULL gate enters the Harvest pool as a new body. potFailsToDormant CONSECUTIVE failed pots flag the seed Dormant (operator revives/expires); a dead seed never kills a living body.
farm.$potGateViews: The pot gate's OWN view floor (owner, 2026-11-19: "lower view baseline"). The scaled bar (0.8 x 400K = 320K) could not be reached at November reach: the median thread on Nov 17-18 got 26K views (32 threads), and September pots, which out-earned covers per view, had median 23-34K. The owner picked 100K from 25K / 50K / 100K on the card. At 320K every pot read as a miss and three misses flag a seed Dormant. Only the view part moves; the money part stays at potGateFactor ($200, 480 clicks, 720 Typefully clicks, or $320 outright). Entry and attempt gates are unchanged. Remove the key to scale views by potGateFactor again.
farm.$potGateCommission: The pot gate's OWN money bar on the views+commission path (owner, 2026-11-19, asked whether the $200 should move too: "drop it to $150"). A pot performs at potGateViews + $150. The other paths keep potGateFactor: 480 Levanta clicks, 720 Typefully clicks, or $320 outright. Remove the key to scale by potGateFactor again ($200).
farm.$potFailsAutoDormant: Owner, 2026-11-19, asked whether a seed should pause by itself after 3 pots with no perform: "make my call - I believe they can all perform. If we added it as a seed they must be at a certain standard. most of time it doesn't work is because our machine didn't write the copy correctly." So false: three consecutive missed pots are REPORTED for the owner and the seed's Status is never changed by the gate. Before reporting a seed as failing, read its missed pots against the origin (hook verbs, adjectives, structure): a pot that drifted is a writing miss, not a seed miss. true restores the automatic Dormant flag.
farm.$coverAsPot: EVERY COVER IS WRITTEN AS A POT (owner, 2026-10-12: "every cover —> now write as pot ... cover —> seed —> pot, we can choose and change from the variables available"; chose "Build now" on the card). The donor is read as an UNNAMED seed: its skeleton (seed-mint's closed vocabulary, never minted, never named, no Seeds row) is the home cell, and the cover is a pot of it, stamped on the spec with the same `dials` ticket a pot carries. As for a seed (docs/seed-dials/README.md), the control `[]` keeps the donor's hook shape and writes NEW items into its skeleton; a 1-2 dial ticket also turns hook components, inside the hook band. Why: a plain cover keeps the donor's items and moves the hook only to 0.85-0.93, so it reads to X as a lightly reworded copy of a post that already went viral (inferred, unverified; the 2026-10-10 verbatim reruns of our own 500k+ bodies did 28-76k against 0.8-4.7M originals). New items make the body ours, and the ticket lets the 48h read be attributed to a named change. WHAT DOES NOT MOVE: the hook gate (hook.coverFloor, measured 2026-09-06 at an 18x reach gap below it), so a dial that touches the hook (topic, count, audience) still has to land the hook in band; a cover that wants a new hook subject is a remix. A cover-pot that clears the full gate is a candidate for /seed-mint by hand-induction, and naming stays the owner's. run-content-packets holds a cover without a ticket at the drafts stop; publish-thread stamps the ticket on the ledger row. on:false restores plain covers.
farm.$coverBodyMax: NEW ITEMS, CHECKED (owner 2026-10-12: "build this", on the gap that "items are new" was a written rule no gate read). A cover-pot's body, tweet 2 onward, may share at most this much with the donor's body, measured as word-4-gram overlap (checks.mjs bodyOverlap, the donor screen's own measure) read in both directions, the higher one counting. Measured 2026-10-12: the three cover-pot trial bodies scored 0-3%; six plain covers from 2026-10-04 scored 15-71%. 0.10 sits between the two. A cover held here kept the donor's items: write new ones into the skeleton.
farm.$phases: Rollout bucket WEIGHTS [cover, harvest, pot], one generation per milestone — normalize by the sum when allocating (the operator's phase-1 numbers total 105, so they are weights, not strict percents). Advance past phase 2 only when >= 1 pot has a Performed verdict (the /farm checkpoint, operator-overridable).

The rollout ramp, by RUN. Weights, not percents — plan-check normalizes each triple by its own sum, which is why phase 1's 75/20/10 totalling 105 is deliberate. Phase 3 was the last one the ramp planned for; phase 4 is an operator decision (2026-09-13) that tilts further off covers and splits the remainder evenly between the two proven lanes. Phase 5 is an operator decision too (2026-09-17, Run 5) and it moves BACK up the cover column, for a supply reason rather than a strategy one: see $phase5.
farm.$phase5: 45/25/30, set by the operator for Run 5 (Fri-Sun 2026-09-18..20). Covers rise because HARVEST CANNOT FILL 30%. pool-probe on 09-17 returned 11 runnable of 27 bodies, and four of those eleven sit at zero hearts, so only SEVEN bodies could take a heart at all; against the 24h cooldown that is 7 x 3 days = 21 body-days total, and a 30% harvest share wanted 20 of them. One refusal at write time and the lane is short. 25% asks for 16 and leaves real slack. The operator repairs the pool separately; when it is repaired this number goes back up, and that is a laws edit, not a --phase flag. The COVER 45 is TWO lanes: half written as covers, half as remixes of the same donors (operator: 'remix the donor'). Remix rows carry bucket 'cover' with lane 'remix', because a fourth bucket would silently break the MIX arithmetic — plan-check sums cover/harvest/pot only, so a remix bucket would inflate the total and report all three lanes short.
farm.$phase6: Owner decision 2026-09-21 for Monday/Tuesday run: cover40/harvest20/seed40. Existing booked content and final account warmups are preserved; requested mix applies to newly allocated money-thread slots.
farm.$phase7: 50/20/30, set by the operator 2026-09-23 for this run (Wed-Fri 2026-09-23..25), in their words: "Let's do 50/20/30". Covers rise again and the pot column comes down from phase 6's 40. HARVEST STAYS AT 20 on the same supply argument as $phase5, and the numbers still say 20: pool-probe on 09-23 returned 13 runnable of 26 bodies, one of those at zero hearts, so 12 bodies can actually take a heart; against the 24h cooldown that is 12 x 3 days = 36 body-days and 63 hearts, which carries 20% (14 slots) with real slack but would be one write-time refusal from short at 30%. The POT COLUMN comes down because 40% of a 72-slot run is ~29 angles in one sitting and every one of them is the operator's creative call; 30% asks for ~22 across the five plantable seeds (olive Active; yarrow, ginger, mango, poppy Approved) and leaves the cover lane, which is the lane that absorbs a shortfall, the room to take it. The checkpoint was read clear before this was set: a pot has Performed, 110 fired.
farm.$excludeTitle: Title regex that bars a draft from Harvest induction outright: reference/infra drafts (LOCKED, [CTA]) and parked work. Burner + client accounts are excluded by roster rule, not by title.

selection.$listicleBoost: Operator 2026-09-21 prefers proven listicle hooks for the first pass of cover selection: their clear numbered promise is easier to preserve while delivering useful points. Raised the cover picker preference from the shared scale value 1.5 to 1.8, without changing plan-week's separate use of that shared value. This is a bounded ranking preference, not a hard quota or a measured claim that listicles convert better. Age-arm, 500k view, burn and overlap screens still decide whether a source may ship; the selection summary reports the actual listicle share for review.
selection.$comment: Donor freshness. viralWindowDays bounds the pool; the half-life tilts INSIDE it, and the floor stops an old-but-excellent donor being zeroed rather than merely outranked. Retuned 2026-08-28 (operator: "prioritize the more recent one"). Half-life 14 -> 7: a fortnight-old donor now needs 4x the reach-and-conversion of a fresh one, where before it needed 2x. Floor 0.4 -> 0.12 because a floor that binds early destroys the tilt it exists to soften — at half-life 5 the old 0.4 floor flattened everything past 6.6 days, so a 7-day donor and a 21-day one scored identically. 7/0.12 stays monotonic out to 21 days and only flattens beyond that. Window 21 -> 30 to widen the POOL; ranking, not the window, is what keeps the batch fresh.
selection.$donorOverlapWarn: Share of a donor's own word-4-grams that already appear in another donor on the same day's slate. Added 2026-08-29 after the 08-31 slate handed two accounts the same recycled nitric-oxide thread, with two byte-identical tweet bodies, and it was caught only because the second one was written by hand and read oddly. Measured on that slate: real collisions scored 29-61%, the donors we kept scored 0-11%, and unrelated donors score 0. A WARNING, never a block -- two threads can share a mechanism honestly, and the caller is a human who can read both.
selection.$recencyRetune20260908: MEASURED, and it moves the two numbers that were doing the most damage. Donor age against OUR result, current regime, 121 covers: 0-7d median 285,529 impressions / 161 clicks / $158.66 a thread · 7-14d 118,944 / 80 / $138.12 · 14-30d 107,489 / 64 / $54.79 · 30-90d 100,165 / 74 / $51.56 · 90d+ 32,098 / 14 / $7.25 (n=4). THE 30-90 DAY BAND MEASURES EQUAL TO 14-30. There is no cliff at the window edge, and the old curve put an 8.3x one there: 0.5^(30/7) floors instantly, so every donor past ~25 days sat at 0.12 while a three-day-old sat at 0.74. That is why an old thread with extraordinary numbers could never surface, which is exactly what the operator reported. Fitting both columns gives half-life ~14 days decaying to a plateau ~0.33, not 7 and 0.12. Raising the floor also RE-BALANCES the whole formula: the age term now swings 3x instead of 8.3x, so reachTiers (up to 2x) and intent (up to 1.4x) can actually decide a ranking instead of being rounding errors.
selection.$archiveDecay: The extra handicap past archiveStepDays. Operator 2026-09-08 chose the 365-day vault KNOWING the 90-365 slice is unproven: the current regime has n=4 there, and the all-time numbers that look catastrophic ($1.91-$2.32 a thread) are almost entirely the retired evergreen lane, which selected on allTimeFloor 2M and is the same artefact that faked the donor-size finding. So this is a declared bet, priced conservatively rather than excluded, and donor-arm.mjs reports the slice separately so it can be settled instead of argued.
selection.$archiveDecay20260917: THE 90-DAY CLIFF RESTED ON n=7, AND IT WAS HIDING A REAL WALL 275 DAYS FURTHER OUT. Operator asked for a deliberate blend of trending and resurfaced evergreen winners, and named three writers to try. Re-measuring donor age against OUR result, current regime, 227 matured covers: 0-7d n=69 244,483 imp $136.64 · 8-14d n=47 155,846 $116.22 · 15-30d n=40 109,491 $66.85 · 31-60d n=30 85,091 $58.19 · 61-90d n=4 69,775 $81.34 · 91-150d n=2 132,129 $9.61 · 151-240d n=5 52,270 $24.65 · 241-365d n=0 · 366d+ n=17 11,926 $3.24. The `deep-archive` headline of 25 covers at $7.90 was SEVENTEEN covers past 365 days, which this ranking never picked, plus seven inside it. So the step that has been flattening everything from 91 to 365 days to a constant 0.15 was fitted on seven covers, and the 241-365 band has literally never been tried. Replaced by a continued exponential to a lower plateau: an evergreen donor now ranks BELOW every fresh one and can still be reordered by reach and merit against its own band, which a constant cannot do.
selection.$evergreenFloor: The plateau the 91-365d band decays toward, in place of the flat 0.15 step. 0.5^(age/14) is far below this by 91 days, so the floor is what actually binds and the band spans 0.15 down to 0.10 — narrow on purpose. It is not the tilt that decides whether an evergreen donor ships; evergreenShare is, and it reserves the slots so the bet gets measured instead of being outranked into never happening.
selection.$evergreenShare: Share of a run's cover slots reserved for donors past archiveStepDays — the third arm, after fresh (<=30d) and archive (31-90d). Operator 2026-09-17: "a great blend between what is trending, which is content that is recently performing, but we are also resurfacing evergreen posts from before. We know, fundamentally, they have something that helped them go viral before." Same shape as archiveShare and explorationShare: it never outranks merit, it only guarantees the rows exist. 0.15 of 11 picks is between one and two a day, which is the smallest slate that produces a readable n inside a month and the largest that cannot wreck a run if the band is as bad as 366d+ turned out to be. Read it back with donor-arm.mjs. 0 turns the arm off.
selection.$topicSpread: NOVELTY (operator 2026-09-08, 'add novelty, gently'). 165 current-regime covers came from 104 donors -- 1.59 covers per donor -- and 85% of them landed in five topic buckets: general 32%, stress 17%, heart 15%, bloodsugar 11%, fitness 10%, with seven more topics sharing the last 15%. Repetition at that rate is what stops NEW harvest bodies appearing, because the funnel can only find what it tests. Reuses spreadFactor, the same tilt product diversity already uses, so there is one idiom for 'this has been picked enough lately'. Gently is the point: halving every six covers keeps the money topics leading and buys two or three exploratory slots a run rather than abandoning what converts.
selection.$topicMemory: WIDEN THE LANE (operator 2026-09-09). topicSpread was scoped to one batch, so topicUses started EMPTY every run: each run reopened with every topic at full novelty, took the money topics first because they carry the intent multiplier, and reproduced the same mix. Measured over the 20 days to 09-09: sleep 33%, stress 15%, heart 10%, fitness 10%, bloodsugar 6% -- 74% of covers in five buckets, while skin (55 plug-able products) took 5% and joint (33) took 2%. Halving every six covers inside a day cannot fix a bias that resets daily. topicMemory() seeds the tally from the ledger's own topic stamp, half-life decayed over topicMemoryDays, so a subject worked hard last week still costs something today. The tilt stays BOUNDED by topicSpreadFloor: at these volumes all five leaders sit at the 0.4 floor together and the cold topics at 0.8-0.95, a ~2x tilt that intent (up to 1.4x) and reach (up to 2x) can still overcome -- the operator's rule is that the five main topics keep their common use, so this biases and never bans.
selection.$explorationShare: The FLOOR on diversity, where topicMemory is only the tilt. Share of a day's picks reserved for COLD topics -- anything outside the hotTopicCount leaders by recent weight, derived from the mix rather than listed so the definition follows reality. Same shape as archiveShare: it never outranks merit, it only guarantees the exploratory slots exist on a day when the leaders would otherwise take everything. Safe because every one of the 13 topics can be monetized -- verified 2026-09-09 against 306 products, thinnest testosterone/liver at 3, richest skin 55 and joint 33, so an exploration slot can always carry a plug. 0 turns the arm off.
selection.$viewFloor: Operator 2026-09-10, twice and unambiguously: "floor must be 500k from now". A donor under 500k is not selected, full stop — supply is not the constraint (104 donors sat at 500k+ inside 30 days on the day this was set, 54 of them usable once oncology and off-niche were dropped, the freshest 1-2 days old at 1.3M and 2.2M), so there is no reason to spend a slot below the bar. WHAT THIS COSTS, recorded because it was measured and the operator overrode it knowingly: the earlier 250k floor existed so a donor collected at 250k could be re-read at 800k a fortnight later, since the scraper updates Impressions in place; and in the then-current regime the 250k-500k band posted the HIGHEST median reach of any band (307k, n=16). Against that, NO donor virality metric predicted our result at all (donor views r=-0.083 against our impressions), so the band advantage was never a strong signal either. Raising the floor shrinks the 30-day selection pool roughly 122 -> 84. The scrape is unaffected: nothing else reads this number, so sub-500k donors still enter the table and can still rise past the bar and become selectable.
selection.$reachTiers: Donor reach as a PRIORITY, [minViews, multiplier] descending. This is an operator preference and NOT a measured effect, and this file should say so plainly. Across 387 matured covers whose donor was inside the 30-day window, NO donor virality metric predicts our result: donor views r=-0.083 against our impressions, -0.135 clicks, -0.184 commission; bookmarks -0.087; likes -0.068; comments -0.220; retweet rate -0.070; engagement rate -0.067; thread retention +0.067; thread length +0.052. In the current regime the 250k-500k band posted the HIGHEST median reach of any band (307k, n=16). An earlier read showing a clean monotone decline with donor size was an ARTEFACT of the retired all-time evergreen lane, whose donors had a median age of 378 days -- it measured the lane, not the size. So these multipliers buy the ordering the operator asked for, not performance the data promises; the honest test is the archive arm below plus a re-read of this correlation once a few hundred covers have shipped under it. Replaces log10(views), which spanned 5.40 at 250k to 6.70 at 5M -- a 1.24x range against recency's 8.3x, so reach was decorative rather than weighted.
